pages.x: In 745 BC Tiglath-Pileser III seized the throne of Assyria, in northern Iraq, in a revolt. He built a standing army of iron-armed infantry, chariots, cavalry and siege engines, and turned it west against the kingdoms of Syria and the Levant. Conquered peoples were deported by the tens of thousands, to break their will to rebel.

Far up the Nile, in Nubia, the kings of Kush ruled from Napata, below the holy mountain of Jebel Barkal. They worshipped Egypt's god Amun, and saw themselves as the true heirs of the pharaohs. Around 728 BC King Piye sailed north, stormed Memphis, and made the princes of a divided Egypt kneel to him.

In 722 BC the Assyrians took Samaria, capital of the kingdom of Israel, after a long siege, and carried off its people, the ten lost tribes of later legend. When Gaza rebelled with help from Egypt, Sargon II beat the rebels and an Egyptian army at Raphia, in 720 BC: the first clash between the two powers.

In 701 BC King Hezekiah of Judah rebelled, counting on Egypt. Sennacherib swept down the coast, beat a Kushite and Egyptian army, and stormed the city of Lachish, a siege he had carved in stone on the walls of his palace at Nineveh. Then he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem, he boasted, like a bird in a cage.

Jerusalem was not taken. Sennacherib's own records say that Hezekiah paid a huge tribute of gold and silver. The Bible says that an angel of the Lord struck down 185,000 Assyrians in a night, and the Greek historian Herodotus heard that mice had gnawed through the bowstrings of an Assyrian army in Egypt.

Taharqa, the greatest of the Kushite pharaohs, built temples from Nubia to the Nile delta, and kept stirring up revolt in the Levant. In 674 BC he threw back an Assyrian invasion. But in 671 BC Esarhaddon crossed Sinai with water carried by Arab camels and took Memphis, and Taharqa fled south, leaving his son a captive.

The Kushites came back again and again. In 663 BC, when Taharqa's successor retook Memphis, the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal sent a great army up the Nile and sacked Thebes, the holy city of Amun, carrying off its treasure and two great obelisks. The Hebrew prophet Nahum remembered its fall.

Kush withdrew to Nubia for good, and its kings ruled on at Napata and later Meroë for almost a thousand years, building pyramids of their own. Assyria had overreached: within about fifty years Egypt and Babylon broke free, and in 612 BC Nineveh itself fell.
pts: Eighty years of war over the Levant
Israel fell in 722 BC, Thebes in 663 BC
